clue.text: Drink squash otherwise he'll clamp down

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
to squash something is to press it
or, as in 'pay or else', means otherwise

explanation.surface: A threat: drink up the squash, or someone will crack down on you.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who suppresses things forcibly holds them down, as a regime crushes dissent.

clue.text: Make robotic car, one of a pair

parts.note: an auto is an American word for a motor car
a mate is one of a matched pair, like a sock's partner

explanation.surface: Someone turns a car, one of two, into a robot.
explanation.definitionFit: To automate a task is to hand it over to machines, making it work like a robot.

clue.text: I won't win any tricks from one who's selfish and base

parts.note: a miser hoards money and will not share it
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A card player confesses to losing every trick, playing against someone mean and low.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as solo whist, a player who calls misère undertakes to lose every trick, so the call itself says 'I won't win any tricks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Misère is the bid in solo whist where the caller promises to take no tricks at all.

clue.text: Entering appeal against covered walk

indicators.note: entering tells us one piece goes into the middle of the other here

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
to can mean against, as in a ladder set to the wall

explanation.surface: Someone lodges an appeal against a planned covered walkway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' puts TO inside SA. A stoa is a roofed colonnade in ancient Greek architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a Greek portico, a roofed colonnade for strolling in the shade.

clue.text: Mysterious artist sporting an eyepiece

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so one piece is worn around the other in this clue

parts.note: an ocular is the eyepiece lens of a microscope or telescope
RA stands for Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: An enigmatic painter wears a monocle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' puts RA inside OCULAR. The artist is the one wearing the eyepiece, but in the letters the eyepiece wraps the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular sayings are like an oracle's: obscure, cryptic and hard to interpret.

clue.text: Scrambled o'er nun in cell

indicators.note: scrambled tells us the letters of the next words are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, the poetic form of over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nun clambers over something in her convent cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' rearranges O'ER and NUN (OERNUN). 'Cell' looks like a nun's room; it is a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is the basic cell of the nervous system that carries nerve impulses.

clue.text: Anybody out of state capital?

indicators.note: out of tells us the state's letters are taken away from the first word

parts.note: anyone means anybody
NY is the abbreviation for New York State

explanation.surface: A question about whether anybody has left the state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' removes NY from ANYONE. 'Capital' is the old British exclamation meaning excellent, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital as an adjective is old-fashioned praise meaning first-rate, the same as A1.

clue.text: African heard coming after Yankee

definitions.meaning: a member of a Bantu people of South Africa
in the radio spelling alphabet spoken over the air, the code word for Z follows Yankee for Y

explanation.definitionFit: The name of the South African people is also the radio code word for the letter Z, which follows Y's Yankee.

clue.text: Atkinson follows footballers with iron protein

indicators.note: follows puts the manager's name after the other pieces

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club, called Inter
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Ron Atkinson is a former English football manager and pundit

explanation.surface: A football manager trails after a team armed with iron, perhaps in a diet supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: Interferon is a protein made by cells to fight viruses.

clue.text: End of allegiance after mates do this?

definitions.text: End of allegiance after mates do this?

indicators.note: after places the closing letter behind the plural word for mates

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a mate or colleague

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of allegiance

explanation.surface: When friends fall out, their loyalty is over.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue says that allegiance ends when friends turn against each other. OPPO is British slang for a friend or partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends who set themselves against each other end their loyalty, which is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Doomed defendant's gripping resistance

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the defendant's letters hold the resistance letter

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial; the 's is a link meaning has
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A doomed man in the dock clings to his defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' puts R inside ACCUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means under a curse, and so doomed to misfortune.

clue.text: Asian born outside borders

indicators.note: outside means the word for born goes around the word for borders

parts.note: née, meaning born, introduces a woman's maiden name
pales are boundaries, as in beyond the pale

explanation.surface: An Asian person was born beyond the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' puts NEE around PALES. A pale is a fence or boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nepal, the Himalayan country, is an Asian.

clue.text: Vote to expel, with lecturer taking place of judge

indicators.note: taking place of signals one letter swapped in for another

parts.note: to eject someone is to expel them

explanation.surface: A move to throw out a judge, with a lecturer stepping in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking place of' puts L in where J was, so EJECT becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose by ballot, casting a vote for someone.

clue.text: 8's third extended measure

parts.note: the third letter of 8 across is L, the standard abbreviation for a unit of size; extended to its full word it gives the measurement

explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to 8 across: its third letter, L, is the usual abbreviation for this measurement, and 'extended' asks for the abbreviation written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is a measure of how far something extends from end to end.

clue.text: Destroying rabid pointer dog

indicators.note: rabid means frenzied, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mad gun dog is wrecking everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabid' rearranges POINTER and DOG (POINTERDOG).
explanation.definitionFit: Torpedoing a plan wrecks it, as a torpedo sinks a ship.

clue.text: Gangway short of one inch

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: an aisle is a gangway between seats
a, as in a single item, means one

explanation.surface: A passageway falls short by a single inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' removes A from AISLE. Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch is a small island, so it means a small piece of land in water.

clue.text: fleece

annotationWithheld.why: clue held only as 'fleece' (5); the newspaper text has lost the wordplay (the blog says it was A inside SHER, the actor Antony Sher) and the full clue cannot be found

clue.text: Odds on animated exercise initially accelerating pulse?

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
lit, as in lit up, means lively or animated
PE is physical education, exercise at school

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of accelerating

explanation.surface: The odds on someone getting their heart rate going with exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is the pulse that means peas, beans and lentils; the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, and a split pea is one such dried seed.

clue.text: Hair style for faint hearted revolutionary is too much

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards
hearted points to letters at the heart of the words for faint

explanation.surface: This bushy hair style would be too much for a timid revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearted' takes ORFA from the middle of 'for faint', and 'revolutionary' turns it round. 'Revolutionary' looks like a person in the surface; here it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy style of naturally curly hair.

clue.text: Cupid again included in endless military display

indicators.note: included in means the word for again goes inside the other piece
endless means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a tattoo is an evening military show with music and marching
more, as in once more, means again

explanation.surface: A cherub appears once more in a military parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' turns TATTOO into ATTO, and 'included in' puts MORE inside it. An amoretto is a little Cupid in art.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a cherub, a small winged figure of the love god in Renaissance painting.

clue.text: Club finally changing sides? That's foolish talk

indicators.note: changing sides at the end means swapping the last letter, right for left

parts.note: a driver is a golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: A golf club's last-minute switch of allegiance is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally changing sides' swaps the final R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is silly, meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Spectator's opinion about to be reversed

parts.note: a view is an opinion

indicators.note: to be reversed tells us the short word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A spectator's view is about to be overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be reversed' turns RE into ER. The 's after Spectator stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewer is someone who watches, the same as an onlooker at a show.

clue.text: Drink dry what's found in the kitchen

parts.note: tea is a drink
to towel something is to dry it

explanation.surface: Have a cuppa and wipe up: a kitchen scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea towel is a cloth for drying dishes, kept in the kitchen.

clue.text: Total confusion about chapter she wrote

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go around the chapter letter
confusion means a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Total chaos surrounds a chapter by a woman author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusion' rearranges TOTAL into ALTOT, and 'about' puts it around C. Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist who wrote Little Women.

clue.text: Choose to keep Conservative in charge as he favours the best of methods

definitions.text: he favours the best of methods

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the vote word holds the party letter

parts.note: to elect is to choose

explanation.surface: A voter picks a Tory boss because he likes the best of every approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To keep' puts C inside ELECT, then IC follows. Here the answer is a noun: a person who borrows what is best from many sources.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclectic picks and mixes the best ideas from many different schools.

clue.text: Two thirds of root vegetable in boggy ground

indicators.note: two thirds of means the last third of the vegetable's letters are dropped

parts.note: a carrot is an orange root vegetable

explanation.surface: Most of a carrot lies in marshy soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two thirds of' keeps the first four of the six letters, dropping OT. Carr is fen woodland, a northern English word.
explanation.definitionFit: A carr is waterlogged fenland overgrown with trees such as alder or willow.

clue.text: Stuff for runner

definitions.meaning: to stuff is to pack in tightly, or revise hard
Steve ..., the British middle-distance runner of the 1980s

explanation.definitionFit: To stuff is to force in tightly, and Steve Cram was a British world-record miler.

clue.text: Aromatic compound could bring you closer

indicators.note: could bring you hints that the following letters can be reworked to give something new

explanation.surface: Some aromatic chemical might draw you nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could bring you' rearranges CLOSER. Cresol is a coal-tar chemical used as a disinfectant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cresol is an aromatic organic chemical, a methylated phenol used in disinfectants.

clue.text: Digression is so unimportant

definitions.meaning: a digression wanders off the point, so it is beside the matter

explanation.definitionFit: A digression is off-topic, beside the point, and something beside the point is of no consequence.

clue.text: Minute Aussie can leave Navy

indicators.note: leave means go away, so the navy letter is taken out

parts.note: a tinny is Australian slang for a can of beer

explanation.surface: An Australian beer can briefly leaves the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' removes one N from TINNY. 'Minute' looks like a unit of time; it is the adjective meaning very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute (pronounced my-NEWT) means extremely small.
